title: 'Oddball' test lets us glimpse how monkeys see the world | New Scientist
description: Compared with humans, macaques are more likely to miss the bigger picture, but are also less confused by flipped images
author: Jo Marchant

title: Predatory amphibians swam the seas 237 million years ago | New Scientist
description: Until now, it was thought that the squishy, permeable skin of amphibians was unsuited for marine life because it would absorb too much salt from sea water – but a fossil found in China upends that view
author: James Woodford

title: Robotic dog controlled with a computer powered by human blood cells | New Scientist
description: A start-up has already used a biological computer to play Pong, and now the firm says the technology can be used to control robots
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Satellites show some of the strongest evidence the AMOC is weakening | New Scientist
description: The crucial Atlantic current system that brings warmth to Europe has slowed 14 per cent in 30 years, according to an analysis of how much heat the ocean is releasing to the atmosphere
author: Alec Luhn

title: Personalised cancer vaccine expected to be approved next year | New Scientist
description: A bespoke vaccine that is tailored to target an individual's unique skin cancer reduced rates of recurrence or death in a late-stage trial, making an approval expected
author: Carissa Wong

title: Brazil presidential election dogged by alleged bias by Meta AI tools | New Scientist
description: Supporters of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva have accused Meta of interfering in Brazil’s election by making it easier to generate campaign content promoting his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro
author: Luke Taylor
